title: Vela Metrics POC orientation and success plan
summary: Orientation and success plan for a 6-week POC with VelaMetrics to validate a hosted Redwood Inference pipeline for enterprise-scale document search + automated executive summaries of earnings reports.
primary_customer_contact: Alyssa Tran (VelaMetrics, Head of Data Products)
use_case_description: Replace ad-hoc keyword search + manual summarization with a semantic vector search layer + extractive+abstractive summarization pipeline to speed analyst workflows and reduce time-to-insight for quarterly earnings analysis.
objectives: Demonstrate semantic search relevance improvement vs current Elasticsearch baseline
Prove automated executive summary quality acceptable for analyst triage
Validate latency and throughput targets on Redwood hosted API under realistic load
Estimate per-report token cost and propose optimizations (caching, batching, quantized model recommendations)
scope_inclusions: Ingest 3 months of VelaMetrics financial reports (approx 3k documents, ~8M tokens)
Build a retrieval pipeline using Redwood embeddings + Redis vector store (customer-managed) for the POC
Implement a two-step summary flow: extract top-K passages -> abstractive rewrite via Redwood chat model
Run a blind relevance evaluation (50 sample queries) and summary quality review with VelaMetrics analyst panel
out_of_scope: SLA or dedicated capacity commitments (this POC uses hosted shared capacity)
acceptance_criteria: Search: semantic precision@10 >= 0.80 vs baseline precision@10 (measured on 50 labeled queries)
Summaries: median analyst rating >= 3.5 / 5 for usefulness and faithfulness on a 30-sample test set
Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end for summary pipeline <= 1200ms for short reports (<= 2k tokens) and <= 2500ms for long reports (<=10k tokens) during 1x baseline traffic
Throughput: sustained 60 summarize requests/minute without error rate > 1%
Cost: estimated per-report token cost <= 50% of prototyped baseline after applying candidate optimizations
Operational: reproducible deploy steps in repo and a short runbook for on-call handoff
metrics_and_evals: Summary quality: analyst Likert (usefulness, faithfulness), ROUGE-L as automated signal
Performance: median and p95 latency, error rate, tokens per request
Cost: tokens consumed and estimated USD cost at hosted API rates
Reliability: % successful requests over test window and transient error analysis
kickoff_workshop_agenda: 20m — Customer environment overview, security and network constraints
30m — Data shape walk-through (example docs, sizes, sensitive fields)
25m — Proposed architecture: embeddings -> vector store -> retriever -> summary model
15m — Success criteria and evaluation plan review
20m — Ops constraints: auth, VPC, KMS, and logging requirements
15m — Timeline, checkpoints, ownership, and next steps
10m — Open Q&A and immediate action items
timeline_milestones: Week 0: Kickoff workshop and environment access
Week 1: Data ingestion proof-of-concept + skeleton pipeline deployed
Week 2: Embedding index built + baseline retrieval evaluation
Week 3: Summary flow implemented and smoke-tested
Week 5: Performance/load test and cost tuning suggestions
Week 6: Final evaluation, handoff demo, and recommended next steps (dedicated vs private)
technical_requirements: Redwood API key (test project) with token ceilings shared by SE team
Customer-managed Redis vector store endpoint (or provisioned ephemeral cluster for POC)
S3 access or secure file share for 3 months of reports
Sample anonymization script if any PHI/PII is present
Access to customer dev Slack channel and a Linera/Linear or Jira epic for tracking
data_requirements: Representative corpus: 3 months of PDFs and converted text (~3k docs)
Label set: 50 queries with canonical relevant doc lists for relevance eval
Summary set: 30 documents with human-written reference executive summaries
Data retention window for POC logs: 14 days (customer-approved)
roles_and_contacts: Redwood SE (POC lead): Priya Raman — priya@redwood.ai
Redwood Platform Eng (ops contact): Luis Ortega — luis@redwood.ai
VelaMetrics Data Eng: Mark Li — mark@velametrics.com
risks_and_mitigations: Data sensitivity: if PHI/PII found, pause ingestion and run anonymization; consult security contact
Hotspot costs: enable request sampling and small-scale performance tests before full ingestion
Latency spikes under load: recommend fallback to shallow extract-only summaries and smaller model variant
Index freshness concerns: limit POC to snapshot corpus and document the delta plan for production
success_checklist: All access granted and sample corpus ingested
Baseline search and summary results documented and reproducible
Acceptance criteria met or a documented mitigation plan exists for shortfalls
Runbook + demo deck delivered and scheduled with Vela execs
Cost/ops recommendation memo delivered to Vela metrics team
notes_and_open_questions: Customer to confirm whether monthly PII scan is required during POC (Action: Alyssa)
Decide vector store option: customer-managed Redis vs Redwood-managed ephemeral cluster
Clarify which 3rd-party icons/logos can be used in final demo deck
Ask Vela whether there are regulatory constraints for storing raw PDFs outside their VPC
